brief.headline: Trade faster payment (15 days earlier) for a ₹61.76 L annual price cut — we're 1.36% of their sales and they carry heavy debt

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 2–3% price reduction in exchange for paying 15 days faster
priceAsk.target: ₹61.76 L annual saving (the value of paying 15 days earlier)
priceAsk.basis: Our current ₹66.48/KG sits in the market-fair band (₹60–81/kg typical ₹66–73/kg) but above the India export benchmark of 42.95 ₹/kg. Paying them 15 days faster frees up ₹61.76 L in cash for us — ask them to share that benefit through a matching price cut, given they owe 2.25x their own cash and value faster payment.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days earlier (cut from 30 days to 15 days after receipt) in exchange for the price reduction
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹61.76 L freed up for us annually if we move to 15-day faster terms

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji keeps only 2.3% of every ₹100 they sell as profit, so there's little room for a hard price squeeze without risking supply. However, they owe 2.25x their own cash (₹238.85 Cr total debt), which means cash is valuable to them — they'll care about getting paid faster. We buy ₹15.03 Cr a year from them, which is 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr in sales — a meaningful customer they won't want to lose. Use that size to trade payment speed for a price cut, not to demand a discount that could hurt a tight-margin supplier.

evidence.point: We are a big customer — our spend is a real chunk of their business
evidence.figure: ₹15.03 Cr annual spend = 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr revenue

evidence.point: They run on thin margins — little profit cushion for a straight price cut
They carry heavy debt — cash matters to them
evidence.figure: Debt is 2.25x their equity; total owed ₹238.85 Cr

evidence.point: Our price sits in the market-fair zone but above the export benchmark
evidence.figure: We pay ₹66.48/KG; market band ₹60–81/kg typical ₹66–73/kg; India export unit value 42.95 ₹/kg

evidence.point: Faster payment is worth real money to us
evidence.figure: Paying 15 days earlier frees ₹61.76 L for us annually

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker with ₹2359.06 Cr revenue and a B (62/100) health score — a drop-in alternate for dextrose with better financial strength than Sayaji

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore maize wet-miller making Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade) — exact form match; confirm IP monograph CoA before switching

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (₹842.97 Cr revenue, C health score) with growing dextrose capacity

risks: Their D (21/100) health score and 2.25x debt load mean supply stability is a watch-out — don't push so hard you tip a fragile supplier; frame the ask as a partnership (we pay faster, they cut price)
We already pay the best price we have for Dextrose (₹66.48/KG) across all our vendors, so there's no internal gap to close — the room is in trading payment terms, not proving we overpay
Their thin 2.3% margin leaves little cushion — if they reject the price cut, pivot to asking for locked-in volume commitment or freight absorption instead
Market backups like Gujarat Ambuja, Roquette India and Ingredion India exist but are leads to qualify (verify pharma-grade CoA, MOQ, price) — not drop-in alternatives today
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to explore paying you 15 days faster — that's worth ₹61.76 lakh a year to us, and we believe it's valuable to you too given your scale; in return, we're looking for a 2–3% price reduction to share that benefit.
